**Brief Description of the Idea**

Securities fraud in India has moved beyond crude scams. The BSE CEO deepfake that surfaced in January 2026 — pushing fake stock tips — was flagged, taken down, and then resurfaced in March through WhatsApp forwards. Deloitte and McAfee estimate deepfake-driven financial fraud has grown over 550% since 2019, with projected losses touching ₹70,000 crore. Meanwhile, SEBI's November 2025 advisory warned that scammers are actively impersonating registered intermediaries, and the May 2026 mandate now requires intermediaries to display verifiable registration details on social media. The problem is clear — and it has two sides that need solving together.

PRAMAAN-SHIELD tackles both.

We've built a three-pillar trust engine that covers the full investor protection journey — from catch**ing fakes to proving what's genuine to helping users report fraud in seconds:**

**Pillar A — Detection (Is this fake?)** When a retail investor receives a suspicious message, email, voice note, or video, they forward it to PRAMAAN-SHIELD through our web app or Telegram bot. The system runs it through a layered pipeline: first, a perceptual-hash check against a registry of known fakes (this catches resurfaced content in under 50 milliseconds — no ML needed, purely deterministic). If the content is new, it goes through our text/phishing classifier (urgency pattern detection, AI-generated text analysis, domain typosquatting checks against 200+ legitimate Indian broker and exchange domains), voice anti-spoofing models (AASIST and RawNet2, which are purpose-built for this), or video deepfake analysis (frame-level CNN with temporal consistency checks). All of this runs in parallel with a SEBI intermediary registry cross-check — so if someone claims to be a registered broker, we verify that claim on the spot.

**Pillar B — Authentication (Is this real?)** Detection alone creates an arms race — every time models improve, so do deepfakes. That's why PRAMAAN-SHIELD also gives SEBI, stock exchanges, and registered intermediaries a way to cryptographically sign their official communications. We use ECDSA digital signatures embedded in a QR code, aligned with the C2PA Content Credentials standard (the same framework Adobe, Microsoft, and BBC use for content provenance). When an investor receives a communication with a PRAMAAN Seal, they scan the QR code and get a deterministic yes-or-no answer: is the signature valid, is the content untampered, and is the issuing entity registered with SEBI? No AI confidence scores, no false positives — just cryptographic proof.

This directly addresses the gap SEBI has flagged: there is currently no mechanism for an ordinary investor to verify whether a circular or press release actually came from an official source.

**Pillar C — Redressal (What do I do about it?)** Most retail investors don't even know SEBI SCORES exists, and filing a complaint takes 30+ minutes of manual effort. When PRAMAAN-SHIELD flags content as suspicious, it offers one-tap complaint generation — pre-filled templates for both SEBI SCORES and cybercrime.gov.in (1930 helpline format), with evidence automatically attached: content hash, AI analysis breakdown, timestamps, and entity verification results. The investor reviews, taps submit, and the complaint is ready. We don't claim auto-submission (SEBI SCORES has no public API), but we cut filing time from half an hour to under a minute.

Everything comes together in a single **Trust Score (0–100)** with a plain-language explainability breakdown. The investor sees one clear answer — not four disconnected tool outputs — along with exactly which checks fired and why. Output is bilingual (Hindi and English) because our target user is the first-generation retail investor getting scam messages on WhatsApp, not a cybersecurity analyst sitting in a SOC.

**Who uses it:**

* **Retail investors** — free web app and Telegram bot for forwarding anything suspicious and getting an instant verdict  
* **Brokers and intermediaries** — API to screen client-facing communications before they go out  
* **SEBI, exchanges, and listed companies** — signing portal for issuing PRAMAAN Seals on official communications

**Proposed Solution – Business Model / Commercial Potential**

PRAMAAN-SHIELD is designed to be both a public good and a sustainable platform:

**For retail investors (B2C):** The web app and Telegram bot are free to use. This serves two purposes — it directly protects the most vulnerable user segment, and every scan adds to the flagged-content dataset, which improves detection accuracy over time. We see this as the trust-building layer that drives organic adoption.

**For brokers and intermediaries (B2B):** We offer an API subscription for bulk-screening inbound and outbound client communications. Brokers can plug PRAMAAN-SHIELD into their communication pipelines to catch phishing and impersonation attempts before they reach investors. This is a natural SaaS revenue model — per-call or monthly subscription pricing.

**For SEBI and exchanges (B2G):** The PRAMAAN Seal authentication infrastructure can be licensed as the technical backbone for the May 2026 mandate requiring intermediaries to display verifiable registration details. The signing portal, QR-based verification, and registry integration are a ready-made compliance tool.

**Long-term defensibility:** Authentication, unlike detection, requires participation from verified entities — not just end users. Once SEBI or exchanges adopt the Seal framework, that creates a structural moat. We're positioning for a SEBI Innovation Sandbox pilot to validate the approach in a regulated environment before broader rollout

| Cryptography | ECDSA (Python cryptography library) | PRAMAAN Seal signing and verification |
| Hashing | pHash / videohash | Perceptual hash generation for known-fake registry |
| Messaging | python-telegram-bot | Telegram bot interface for investors |

**PRAMAAN Detection Flow — Hash check → Parallel ML analysis → Trust Score → Complaint**

**Detection flow — scanning inbound content:**  
A user submits a suspicious message, email, voice recording, or video through the PRAMAAN-SHIELD web app or Telegram bot. The system processes it through a layered pipeline:  
First, the content is hashed (perceptual hash for images/video, text hash for messages) and checked against a Redis-backed registry of known fakes. If the hash matches within a Hamming distance threshold, the system flags it instantly — typically in under 50 milliseconds — and returns the original flagging date, source, and detection count. No ML inference is needed for known content, which keeps costs low and latency minimal.  
If the content is new, it routes to the appropriate detection module. Text-based content goes through a four-layer pipeline: AI-generated text analysis (perplexity and burstiness scoring), phishing pattern classification, domain and sender verification (typosquatting detection via Levenshtein distance against 200+ legitimate Indian financial domains, plus SPF/DKIM/DMARC validation for raw email inputs), and securities-specific red flag detection (SEBI registry cross-check, urgency pattern scoring, claim verification against authenticated communications).  
Audio content goes through AASIST and RawNet2 anti-spoofing models for voice clone detection. Video content goes through frame-level CNN analysis with temporal consistency checks and biological signal analysis.  
All of these signals run in parallel where possible. The results are aggregated into a weighted Trust Score (0–100) with a full explainability breakdown showing which checks fired, what they found, and how they contributed to the overall score.  
If the Trust Score is below the safety threshold, the user is offered one-tap complaint generation with pre-filled templates for SEBI SCORES and cybercrime.gov.in (1930 format), with the evidence package (content hash, analysis report, timestamps, entity verification results) attached automatically.

**Authentication flow — verifying outbound content:**  
A verified entity — SEBI, a stock exchange, or a registered intermediary — logs into the PRAMAAN-SHIELD signing portal and uploads an official communication (circular, press release, or statement). The system generates a SHA-256 content hash, signs it with the entity's ECDSA private key, attaches a timestamp and the entity's SEBI registration number, and embeds all of this into a QR code.  
When an investor encounters a communication carrying a PRAMAAN Seal, they open the PRAMAAN-SHIELD web app, scan the QR code (or enter the Seal ID manually), and the system performs four deterministic checks: Is the cryptographic signature valid? Does the content hash match (meaning the content hasn't been altered)? Is the issuing entity present in the SEBI intermediary registry? Is the timestamp within a valid range? The result is a clear verified/unverified/tampered verdict with full details.
